text:
mike: Heads up — noticed quotas firing for the wrong org after rapidly switching workspaces in the console.

sami: repro steps?

mike: 1) login as admin
2) open org A
3) switch to org B via quick-switch
4) run a bunch of generator requests through the console's run panel
5) quota usage shows attributed to org A, not B

anna: any stack traces or request headers captured? could be routing affinity sticking somewhere.

mike: here's a request header capture from the edge (sanitized):

```
GET /internal/run HTTP/1.1
Host: console.internal
x-org-id: 9876  # client says 9876 after switch
x-route-affinity: org-2345  # server still routing as 2345
User-Agent: Console/1.4.2
```

anna: that x-route-affinity header shouldn't persist after quick-switch. I think the router's header rewrite wasn't applied on the client-side refactor last week.

julie: @anna that refactor was in canary deploy 2026-03-18 22:14. Rolling it back cleared one report earlier today. Ops, can we confirm if any canaries are still active? :eyes: 

ops-bot: Canary rollout status: router-rewrite-v2 -> 35% in us-west, 0% in eu-west

sami: if affinity header is stale, telemetry pipeline will tag metrics and quota checks will index into wrong org's bucket. two problems: (1) misattribution in analytics (2) real quota enforcement for the wrong tenant. both bad.

mike: exact. customer-facing issue when users hit quota unexpectedly.

anna: quick mitigation: drop x-route-affinity at console edge on any quick-switch event until we fix server rewrite logic. also add a metric that counts header mismatch events.

julie: can someone file a short rollback + mitigation plan? I'll coordinate with SRE to pause canary if we see more hits.

mike: filing brief incident note now, linking logs. I'll include sample trace IDs and customer IDs (sanitized).

sami: follow-up: add an e2e test that switches orgs and asserts headers updated before sending workloads; this should run in CI on router changes.

mike: agreed. I'll draft the PR with test and edge-drop flow and tag @anna for review.

julie: :thumbsup: keep this thread updated with rollout status and any affected customers so support can reach out.
